args.content: # The task sent to the agent ## Situation You are in a checkout of scipy/scipy at the commit BEFORE a pull request was merged. Its change is not in this code: whatever it fixes is still broken here, and whatever it adds -- a function, an argument, a class, a module -- does not exist here yet. There is no network here and no version control. You cannot look the answer up; you have to find it by reading the code. ## How this project runs its tests Runner python -m pytest -v -rA -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short --color=no (no project runner found) Targets pytest node ids (`path::name`) -- `run_tests` takes the file path Your test scipy/stats/tests/test_f2p_scipy__scipy_21700.py Tests already in that directory: scipy/stats/tests/test_axis_nan_policy.py scipy/stats/tests/test_binned_statistic.py scipy/stats/tests/test_censored_data.py Test configuration, verbatim from the checkout: --- pytest.ini [pytest] addopts = -l norecursedirs = doc tools scipy/_lib/array_api_compat scipy/_lib/cobyqa scipy/_lib/highs junit_family=xunit2 filterwarnings = error always::scipy._lib._testutils.FPUModeChangeWarning ignore:.*deprecated and ignored since IPython.*:DeprecationWarning once:.*LAPACK bug 0038.*:RuntimeWarning ignore:can't resolve package from __spec__ or __package__, falling back on __name__ and __path__:ImportWarning ignore:assertions not in test modules or plugins:pytest.PytestConfigWarning ignore:'environmentfilter' is renamed to 'pass_environment' ignore:'contextfunction' is renamed to 'pass_context' ignore:.*The distutils.* is deprecated.*:DeprecationWarning ignore:\s*.*numpy.distutils.*:DeprecationWarning ignore:.*`numpy.core` has been made officially private.*:DeprecationWarning ignore:.*In the future `np.long` will be defined as.*:FutureWarning ignore:.*JAX is multithreaded.*:RuntimeWarning Environment (set in this container): PYTEST_ADDOPTS=--import-mode=importlib: pytest imports each test file by its path, so a test file here cannot use relative imports (`from .x import y`); import from `scipy...` instead. ## What to produce A pull request changes how this library behaves. Your job is to write the regression tests that pin that behaviour down, in `scipy/stats/tests/test_f2p_scipy__scipy_21700.py`: enough to have shown what was wrong or missing before the change, and to catch it if anyone undoes it. One test per behaviour the change settles separately -- as many as the change has, and no more. A test is whatever this project's runner collects: a function in some projects, a method on a test class in others. The briefing above says which, and a test the runner does not collect is not a test. Work out what the code does *now*, what it will do *after* the change, and assert the difference. That difference is the whole subject of the test -- not the surrounding function, and not some other property that happens to be broken at the same time. Not every pull request fixes a bug. A feature adds something that does not exist here yet; a refactor or a speed-up may change little that a caller can see. Look for what does change -- a result for some input, an error raised or no longer raised, a new argument or name that now works. A test that only checks that a private name exists tests the code's spelling, not its behaviour. Some changes are about a situation this container does not have: an optional package that is missing, another version of a library, another platform. Then create that situation inside the test -- for example with pytest's `monkeypatch`, by hiding a module (`monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, "name", None)`) or replacing a value -- and assert what the change does there. The report itself is not the subject. It describes a symptom somebody noticed; what you assert has to be the behaviour underneath it, not the wording of the complaint. What this pull request is about: --- Pull request #21700: ENH: `stats.Mixture`: add mixture distributions for new infrastructure #### What does this implement/fix? This adds `scipy.stats.Mixture`, a class for mixture distributions. *Update: Don't be scared by the line count; almost all of it is just movement of documentation.* ```python3 import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from scipy.stats import Mixture, Normal vars = (Normal(mu=-1.2, sigma=1.1), Normal(mu=1.3, sigma=0.9)) weights = (0.4, 0.6) X = Mixture(vars, weights=weights) x = np.linspace(-5, 5, 300) plt.plot(x, X.pdf(x)) plt.hist(X.sample(10000), density=True, bins=30) plt.show() ``` #### Additional information Questions: - ~~What should the class be called?~~ People seem happy with `Mixture`. - ~~What should the arguments be called? Should the random variables and their probabilities be separate lists (as they are now) or, say, a list of tuples?~~ People seem happy with separate `components` (positional only) and `weights`. - ~~To avoid copy-pasting all the method documentation, I was thinking that this and `ContinuousDistribution` should be a subclass of a new superclass `StatisticalDistribution`, and method documentation would go there. Of course, there will be several other subclasses, like `DiscreteDistribution`, etc. Should that superclass be created in this PR or shall we do a separate PR and rebase this after that merges?~~ I'd like to add `_ProbabilityDistribution` in this PR. Thoughts: - There are many ways of making this more efficient at the cost of extra complexity. Let's keep this simple. - Currently this is only for distributions with scalar shapes (not arrays). Separate PR can extend to array shapes. - I remember a request for zero-inflated distributions. I'd like to enable this by creating a degenerate/Dirac continuous distribution in a follow-up PR. The obvious alternative is to wait until there is a discrete uniform distribution (which could have all its mass at zero). - When there are discrete distributions in the mixture, I suppose the PDF at the support values of the discrete distributions will be infinite? And perhaps this class should _also_ have a PMF method, and the PMF at values that are not in the support of a discrete distribution would be zero? - I'll probably want to test edge behavior with distributions that have finite support (but it doesn't really matter until these are public). - `mode` may not return the global maximum of the PDF. This is [already documented](https://scipy.github.io/devdocs/reference/generated/scipy.stats.Normal.mode.html#scipy.stats.Normal.mode). - See gh-21707, which would allow mixtures to be composed of most existing continuous distributions. With that, supersedes gh-19413. --- ## What this pull request changes ```diff This change touches these files (lines added/removed): scipy/stats/__init__.py (+2/-0) scipy/stats/_distribution_infrastructure.py (+323/-1657) scipy/stats/_probability_distribution.py (+1730/-0) scipy/stats/meson.build (+1/-0) diff --git a/scipy/stats/__init__.py b/scipy/stats/__init__.py index 981ecd697c33e47c2f3f66d70b9331478e35bc57..c4298a172b9329acceed3546829e453eb05b3f0b 100644 --- a/scipy/stats/__init__.py +++ b/scipy/stats/__init__.py @@ -466,6 +466,7 @@ Random Variables :toctree: generated/ Normal + Mixture Quasi-Monte Carlo ================= @@ -635,6 +636,7 @@ from ._fit import fit, goodness_of_fit from ._covariance import Covariance from ._sensitivity_analysis import * from ._survival import * +from ._distribution_infrastructure import Mixture from ._new_distributions import Normal from ._mgc import multiscale_graphcorr diff --git a/scipy/stats/_distribution_infrastructure.py b/scipy/stats/_distribution_infrastructure.py index 5609de7e581019941a1aa6c1f3a52ba5cfd24774..0f70397003bab37235c1b5fb9a6dcb38b3c66aad 100644 --- a/scipy/stats/_distribution_infrastructure.py +++ b/scipy/stats/_distribution_infrastructure.py @@ -11,6 +11,7 @@ from scipy import special from scipy.integrate._tanhsinh import _tanhsinh from scipy.optimize._bracket import _bracket_root, _bracket_minimum from scipy.optimize._chandrupatla import _chandrupatla, _chandrupatla_minimize +from scipy.stats._probability_distribution import _ProbabilityDistribution # in case we need to distinguish between None and not specified # Typically this is used to determine whether the tolerance has been set by the @@ -1398,7 +1399,7 @@ def _generate_example(dist_family): return example -class ContinuousDistribution: +class ContinuousDistribution(_ProbabilityDistribution): r""" Class that represents a continuous statistical distribution. import numpy as np
import pytest
from scipy import stats

def test_mixture_import_and_basic_functionality():
    """
    Test that Mixture can be imported and basic functionality works.
    
    This test will fail before the PR is merged (Mixture doesn't exist)
    and pass after the PR is merged (Mixture exists and works).

    # Try to import Mixture - this should work after the PR
    try:
        from scipy.stats import Mixture
    except ImportError:
        # This is expected before the PR - make it clear what should happen
        pytest.fail("Mixture class not yet implemented in scipy.stats. "

    # If we get here, Mixture exists - test its functionality
    
    # Create two normal distributions
    var1 = Normal(mu=-1.2, sigma=1.1)

    # Create a mixture distribution
    weights = [0.4, 0.6]
    mixture = stats.Mixture([var1, var2], weights=weights)
    
    # Test that we can access components and weights
    assert len(mixture.components) == 2

    assert isinstance(cdf_val, np.ndarray)
    assert cdf_val.shape == x.shape
    assert 0 <= cdf_val <= 1
    
    # Test mean calculation (should work)
    mean_val = mixture.mean()
    assert np.isscalar(mean_val) or mean_val.shape == ()
    
    # Test variance calculation (should work)
    var_val = mixture.variance()
    assert np.isscalar(var_val) or var_val.shape == ()
    
    # Test that it can be sampled
    sample = mixture.sample(100)
    assert sample.shape == (100,)

    and pass after the PR is merged (Mixture exists and works).

    var2 = Normal(mu=1.3, sigma=0.9)
    
    # Create a mixture distribution
    weights = [0.4, 0.6]
    mixture = stats.Mixture([var1, var2], weights=weights)
    
    # Test that we can access components and weights
    assert len(mixture.components) == 2

    # Test variance calculation (should work)
    var_val = mixture.variance()
    assert np.isscalar(var_val) or var_val.shape == ()
    
    # Test that it can be sampled
    sample = mixture.sample(100)
    assert sample.shape == (100,)
